rich_summary: This section depicts the ferocity of Bhishma on the battlefield and the strategic effort to bring him down. Bhishma is portrayed like a blazing fire consuming armies, his arrows devastating thousands of warriors from many kingdoms. Even massive formations collapse before him, and soldiers fear approaching him. Sikhandin advances and wounds Bhishma, but Bhishma refuses to strike back because he remembers Sikhandin’s former femininity. Arjuna urges Sikhandin to press the attack, knowing Bhishma will not fight him fully. Meanwhile Dussasana fights fiercely to shield the grandsire and momentarily holds off the Pandavas until Arjuna defeats him and advances. Duryodhana rallies his troops, proclaiming Bhishma invincible and urging a mass assault on Arjuna. The passage highlights Bhishma’s near-mythic power and the crucial tactic of using Sikhandin to neutralize him.

highlight_spans.why: The opening metaphor portraying Bhishma and his chariot as a raging fire sets the epic tone and frames his destructive power.
Describes Bhishma’s arrows cutting down warriors and formations, emphasizing his overwhelming battlefield dominance.
The pivotal moment where Bhishma refuses to strike Sikhandin because of Sikhandin’s past, creating the strategic weakness the Pandavas exploit.
The emotional and dramatic depiction of Bhishma receiving Sikhandin’s arrows almost cheerfully, underscoring his stoic warrior ethos.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma standing tall on his chariot like a blazing fire, arrows streaming from his bow while fallen warriors and shattered chariots litter the battlefield.
Sikhandin firing arrows into Bhishma’s chest while the grandsire calmly refuses to strike back, Arjuna urging the attack from a nearby chariot driven by Krishna.
Dussasana fiercely battling the Pandavas to shield Bhishma, elephants and horses collapsing around him as arrows fill the sky.
